title: For each k and every sufficiently large n with k dividing ((n-1) choose (k-1)), there is a universal cycle for the k-sub
exact_target: For each fixed subset size and all sufficiently large ground sets, is the necessary divisibility condition sufficient for a cyclic word whose windows represent every subset exactly once?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 3100078 (AMR-030-0078). CC BY 4.0.

Yevgeniy Rudoy, \emph{An inductive approach to constructing universal cycles on the $k$-subsets of $[n]$} (2013 revision), Section1, definition, Lemma1.1 and Chung--Diaconis--Graham conjecture, pages1--2; Section2, cycles and universal cycles, pages3--4.
